Authorize the app via OAuth for the connected person on their own OpenProject instance, with the instance base URL as user input

guide.summary: The app can use OAuth2 authorization code flow to act as the connected person on their own OpenProject instance. The api_v3 scope is the documented standard API scope, and reading work packages also requires the person's account access to view work packages.
guide.recommendation: The app can use OAuth2 authorization code flow to act as the connected person on their own OpenProject instance. The api_v3 scope is the documented standard API scope, and reading work packages also requires the person's account access to view work packages.

findings.title: Authorization code flow with instance-specific OAuth endpoints
findings.detail: The auth URL is the instance host plus /oauth/authorize and the token URL is the instance host plus /oauth/token. The redirect URI must match the OAuth application configuration. The bearer token acts on behalf of the current user.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects its own OpenProject instance using the instance base URL as user input.

evidence.quote: Auth URL: https://example.com/oauth/authorize Access Token URL: https://example.com/oauth/token

https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.

findings.title: api_v3 OAuth scope for the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope. If no scope is checked, api_v3 is assumed by default. It is not specific to the BIM edition.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading work package titles through the standard API v3 endpoints.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Connected person needs account access to view work packages
findings.detail: The list work packages endpoint requires the view work packages permission globally or in any project. The OAuth scope does not add this account permission, so the connected person must already have it.
findings.appliesWhen: The confirmed request says the connected person can already access the work packages.

evidence.quote: Required permission: view work packages (globally or in any project)
Required permission: view work packages

findings.title: Instance administrator must register the OAuth application
findings.detail: OAuth applications are created under Administration, Authentication, OAuth applications. The redirect URL is provided by the client app, and the client ID and secret must be recorded.
findings.appliesWhen: Before a customer instance is connected to the app.

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
Define a Redirect URL where users are redirected to after having authorized OAuth2 access in OpenProject. This URL is provided by your client application. In the case of locally running
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

steps.title: Register the OAuth application on the customer's OpenProject instance
steps.detail: An instance administrator creates a new OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications, adds the app redirect URL, selects the api_v3 scope, and records the Client ID and Client secret. No registration has been performed by this step.
steps.doneWhen: The OAuth application exists with api_v3 scope, a confidential client type, and its Client ID and Client secret are stored securely.

REDIRECT_URI: redirect URL configured in the OAuth application

steps.title: Open the consent URL and verify the callback code
steps.detail: The connected person opens the documented authorization URL on their instance, grants consent, and the browser is redirected to the redirect URI with a code parameter. The app must not treat this as completed without the callback.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URI receives a code parameter after the connected person approves access.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
Request authorization code Request an authorization code. Please adopt the following URL replacing:
In this example we skip that server side implementation and just copy the value of the code parameter from the URL that you see in your browser.

fields: CLIENT_ID: from the registered OAuth application
REDIRECT_URI: must match the registered redirect URL
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the code from the callback at the documented token endpoint using client credentials and the authorization_code grant. This is an unexecuted authorization step until the connected person completes consent.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains access_token, token_type Bearer and refresh_token.

evidence.quote: $ curl --request POST \
--data grant_type = authorization_code \
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

fields: CLIENT_SECRET: stored when the OAuth application was created
AUTHORIZATION_CODE: copied from the redirect URI query string after consent
REDIRECT_URI: same value used in the consent request
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Read the first page of accessible work package titles
steps.detail: Calls the work packages collection with an explicit page size and an empty filter so no default filter silently narrows results. Titles are read from each element's subject. First page of the work packages collection used as the start of pagination.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains _embedded.elements with subject values and _links.nextByOffset when more pages exist. Response contains elements, count, total and nextByOffset when further pages exist. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
offset The page number that is requested from paginated collection Integer when offset based available
nextByOffset Link to retrieve the following page of elements (offset based) when offset based available
optional query JSON specifying filter conditions. Accepts the same format as returned by the queries endpoint. If no filter is to be applied, the client should send an empty array

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
ACCESS_TOKEN: bearer token from the token exchange
filters=[]: empty array disables the default filter
ACCESS_TOKEN: bearer token

steps.title: Follow nextByOffset to read the next page of work package titles
steps.detail: Requests the page referenced by _links.nextByOffset from the prior response, resolved against the same HTTPS instance host, and repeats until nextByOffset is absent or count plus offset covers total.
steps.doneWhen: Repeat while _links.nextByOffset is present; stop when it is absent, meaning the last page has been read. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: nextByOffset Link to retrieve the following page of elements (offset based) when offset based available
offset The page number that is requested from paginated collection Integer when offset based available
this response and action links to retrieve the remaining elements.

fields: NEXT_PAGE_URL: value of _links.nextByOffset.href from the prior response, resolved against the instance HTTPS host
